title: Generated finite-extension polynomial resources
objective: Implement generated FLINT fq_default context and polynomial resources with bulk power-basis coordinate I/O, safe shared-context ownership, resource-to-resource arithmetic, portable correctness, lifecycle fuzzing, and measured production performance

handoff.summary: Generated thread-affine FLINT fq_default resources now provide exact-identity shared contexts, elements, and polynomials with checked bulk word-coordinate ingress, checked coordinate access, copy/equality/arithmetic, full coordinate transfer, deterministic close, source-transparent typed-Python kernels, Sage differentials, sanitizer lifecycle coverage, and measured performance. The implementation fixes fq_default to fq_nmod internally; public mathematical state remains the characteristic, monic irreducible modulus, generator name, and low-to-high power-basis coordinates. At GF(3^2) with 1000 coefficients, bulk ingress is about 0.09 ms and squaring about 0.14 ms; degree-128 export of 5000 coefficients is about 3.4 ms. SJFC is an internal coordinate-transfer frame only, not public standalone serialization: portable serialization remains descriptor plus coordinates at the public layer.
risks: This v1 resource ingress is intentionally word-characteristic only; large-prime coordinates retain the portable path until IntegerBuffer ingress is generated.
The resources are explicitly thread-affine because FLINT context access and non-atomic reference counts are serialized by the owning execution thread.

Closing the public context wrapper while dependents survive temporarily under-reports the shared context allocation; it does not double-count, leak, or free early, and the repository TODO records shared accounting tokens if measured GC pressure warrants them.
Browser/Wasm lowering remains capability-gated (wasm=False); dynamic same-source correctness is tested but FLINT resource publication in Wasm is a later platform lane.
next_steps: Wire public finite-extension polynomial construction and arithmetic to the generated resources so the measured bulk-ingress speedup reaches ordinary Sage.js users.
Represent public serialization as the complete field descriptor plus SJFC-equivalent coordinate content; never treat the coordinate frame alone as field identity.
Run the sanitizer and performance witness on macOS arm64 and Linux arm64, then add the future Wasm resource-lifetime implementation.
Extend exact-integer coordinate ingress for characteristics larger than one machine word.
